phrases: how do i upload my resume
faq.answer:
To upload your resume:
1. Click **Get Started** in the navigation bar
2. On the **Upload Resume** step, click the upload zone or drag & drop your PDF
3. File must be PDF format, max **5MB**

The AI will automatically extract all your skills — it usually takes about 10–15 seconds.

**Gap Analysis** compares your skills (extracted from your resume) against the requirements of a target job.

It produces:
• **Missing skills** — skills the job needs that you don't have yet
• **Partial skills** — skills you have but need to strengthen
• **Satisfied skills** — skills you already have that match the job
• **Match Score** — your overall fit percentage (0–100%)

A higher match score means you're a stronger candidate for that role.

A **Learning Pathway** is a personalised, prioritised sequence of skills to learn — generated from your Gap Analysis.

Each step includes:
• The **skill** to learn
• The **priority** (critical / recommended / optional)
• A linked course from our course library
• Estimated hours to complete

Steps are ordered to maximise your match score improvement fastest.

Here's how to get started with AdaptLearn in **4 steps**:

1. **Upload Resume** → Go to *Get Started* and upload your PDF resume
2. **Pick a Job** → Browse jobs and select your target role
3. **Gap Analysis** → See which skills you're missing for that job
4. **Generate Pathway** → Get your personalised learning plan

Each step builds on the previous one!

To **improve your match score**:

1. **Focus on critical skills** first — these have the biggest impact
2. **Complete pathway steps** — each skill learned increases your score
3. **Update your resume** after gaining new skills — re-run gap analysis
4. **Target partial skills** — strengthening partial matches also boosts your score

Consistently completing pathway steps is the fastest way to increase your match percentage.

**Resume Tips for Tech Roles:**

• **Keep it to 1–2 pages** — concise and focused
• **List specific technologies** — Python, React, AWS etc. (not just 'programming')
• **Quantify achievements** — 'Reduced load time by 40%' beats 'improved performance'
• **Include projects** — personal or open source projects count
• **Match job keywords** — use the same terms the job posting uses
• **PDF format** — always submit as PDF to preserve formatting

**Interview Preparation Guide:**

**Technical:**
• Practice LeetCode / HackerRank (easy → medium)
• Review data structures: arrays, hashmaps, trees, graphs
• Practice system design for senior roles

**Soft Skills:**
• Use the **STAR method** for behavioural questions (Situation, Task, Action, Result)
• Research the company before the interview
• Prepare 2–3 questions to ask the interviewer

**For coding rounds:** Think out loud — explain your approach before coding

**Typical Tech Salaries (USD, varies by location & experience):**

| Role | Entry | Mid | Senior |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frontend Dev | $60K | $90K | $130K+ |
| Backend Dev | $65K | $95K | $140K+ |
| Full Stack | $70K | $100K | $145K+ |
| Data Scientist | $75K | $110K | $155K+ |
| ML Engineer | $85K | $120K | $165K+ |
| DevOps / SRE | $75K | $110K | $150K+ |

*Note: These are US market averages. Rates vary significantly by city and company.*

**How to Switch Careers into Tech:**

1. **Identify your target role** — frontend, backend, data, ML, DevOps?
2. **Build foundation skills** — 3–6 months of focused learning
3. **Build a portfolio** — 2–3 real projects on GitHub
4. **Network** — LinkedIn, local meetups, open source contributions
5. **Apply broadly** — especially to companies with structured new-grad/career-changer programs

**Use AdaptLearn's gap analysis** — pick a job and see exactly what skills you need!

**AdaptLearn** is an AI-powered career coaching platform that helps you bridge the gap between your current skills and your dream job.

**Core features:**
• 🤖 **AI Resume Parsing** — extract skills from your CV automatically
• 📊 **Gap Analysis** — compare your skills to any job's requirements
• 🛤️ **Adaptive Pathway** — personalised learning plan ranked by priority
• 💼 **Job Board** — curated job listings with skill matching
• 📚 **Course Library** — courses mapped to every skill gap
• 🤝 **AI Coach** — that's me! Ask anything career-related

**Python Learning Roadmap:**

**Beginner (1–2 months):**
• Variables, data types, control flow
• Functions, modules, file I/O
• Lists, dicts, sets, tuples

**Intermediate (2–3 months):**
• OOP — classes, inheritance
• Error handling, decorators
• `requests`, `json`, `csv` libraries

**Specialise:**
• **Web** → FastAPI or Django
• **Data** → NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib
• **ML** → scikit-learn, PyTorch
• **Automation** → Selenium, BeautifulSoup

*Recommended: Python Crash Course (book) + freeCodeCamp Python course*

**JavaScript Learning Roadmap:**

**Beginner (1–2 months):**
• Variables, functions, arrays, objects
• DOM manipulation, event handling
• Async JS — callbacks, Promises, async/await

**Intermediate (2–3 months):**
• ES6+ features (arrow functions, destructuring, modules)
• Fetch API, JSON handling
• npm ecosystem

**Frameworks (pick one):**
• **React** — most in-demand, component-based UI
• **Vue** — gentler learning curve
• **Angular** — TypeScript-first, enterprise-friendly

*Start with The Odin Project (free) or javascript.info*

**React Learning Roadmap:**

**Prerequisites:** HTML, CSS, JavaScript fundamentals

**Core React (2–3 months):**
• JSX, components, props, state
• `useEffect`, `useState`, `useRef`, `useContext`
• React Router for navigation
• Fetching data with Axios / Fetch

**Advanced (2–3 months):**
• State management — Zustand or Redux Toolkit
• Performance — `useMemo`, `useCallback`, `React.memo`
• Testing — React Testing Library + Jest
• TypeScript with React

*Best resource: Official React docs (react.dev) — they're excellent!*

**Docker Learning Roadmap:**

**Basics (1 month):**
• What is containerization?
• `docker run`, `pull`, `ps`, `exec`, `logs`
• Writing a `Dockerfile`
• Docker volumes and networks

**Intermediate:**
• `docker-compose` for multi-container apps
• Container registries (Docker Hub, ECR, GCR)
• Multi-stage builds for smaller images

**Advanced:**
• Kubernetes (orchestration at scale)
• Docker security best practices
• CI/CD with Docker

*Free resource: Play with Docker (labs.play-with-docker.com)*

**Staying Consistent with Learning:**

• **2 hours/day beats 14-hour weekend** — consistency > intensity
• **The 25-min Pomodoro** — 25min study, 5min break, repeat
• **Block calendar time** — treat study time like a meeting
• **Track progress** — your AdaptLearn pathway shows your progress!
• **Build → Learn → Build** — apply skills immediately in projects
• **Find a study buddy** — accountability multiplies consistency

*For most career switchers: 6–9 months of consistent learning leads to job-readiness.*

smallTalk.response: I'm an AI assistant — no human on the other end here! 🤖 But I'm trained specifically for career coaching and have full access to your AdaptLearn profile data to give you personalised advice.

Here's what I can help with:

• 📋 **Your skills** — what's on your resume
• 🔍 **Skill gaps** — what you're missing for your target job
• 🛤️ **Learning pathway** — what to study next and in what order
• 📈 **Progress** — how far along your learning plan you are
• 💼 **Jobs** — which jobs match your current skill set
• 📚 **Courses** — recommendations based on your gaps
• 🎯 **Career advice** — interview tips, resume writing, career switching
• ❓ **Platform help** — how to use any AdaptLearn feature

Just ask away!

Why do programmers prefer dark mode?

Because light attracts bugs! 🐛😄

…okay, back to your learning journey. What can I help you with?

It sounds like you need a break — and that's totally okay! 😊

Burnout is real. Take a rest, go for a walk, sleep well.

Remember: **rest is part of the process**. Consistent learning with proper breaks beats pushing through exhaustion every time. You'll come back sharper. 💪

Let me share something:

**Every expert was once a beginner.** The developers you admire didn't wake up knowing this stuff — they showed up every day, made mistakes, and kept going.

You're here, using a platform to close your skill gaps systematically — that already puts you ahead of most people. 🚀

Check your pathway progress — even one completed step is real evidence you're moving forward. What's the next skill you want to tackle?
